---
title: "Structured data (YAML, TOML, XML, RDS, FWF)"
engine: knitr
---

## YAML

Files ending in `.yaml` or `.yml` are read with
[yaml](https://cran.r-project.org/package=yaml). Nested structures are
preserved when the output format supports nesting (JSON, YAML, TOML, XML, RDS);
otherwise they are flattened.

### Reading

```{bash}
rush run -n 'head(df)' config.yaml
```

### Writing

```{bash}
rush run -n -O yaml -o output.yaml 'df' data.csv
```

### Converting (nesting preserved)

```{bash}
rush convert -n -o output.yaml data.json
```

## TOML

Files ending in `.toml` are read with
[RcppTOML](https://cran.r-project.org/package=RcppTOML):

### Reading

```{bash}
rush run -n 'head(df)' config.toml
```

### Writing

```{bash}
rush run -n -O toml -o output.toml 'df' data.csv
```

## XML

Files ending in `.xml` are read with [xml2](https://xml2.r-lib.org/).
Data frames are serialized as rows, with configurable element names.

### Reading

```{bash}
rush run -n 'head(df)' data.xml
```

### Writing

```{bash}
rush run -n -O xml -o output.xml 'df' data.csv
```

### `--output-root` and `--output-record`

Customize the root and record element names (defaults: `root` and `record`):

```{bash}
rush run -n -O xml --output-root plants --output-record observation 'head(df)' data.csv
```

## RDS

R's native serialisation format. Files ending in `.rds` are read with
`readr::read_rds()` and written with `readr::write_rds()`:

### Reading

```{bash}
rush run -n 'head(df)' data.rds
```

### Writing

```{bash}
rush run -n -o output.rds 'df' data.csv
```

## Fixed-width files (FWF)

Files ending in `.fwf` are read with `readr::read_fwf()`. Column positions are
auto-detected. This format is read-only.

### Reading

```{bash}
rush run -n 'head(df)' data.fwf
```

### Using `-F fwf` for files without the `.fwf` extension

```{bash}
rush run -n -F fwf 'head(df)' legacy.txt
```
